summary: Defines an extension to the IMAP LIST command so a client can ask for mailbox annotations (metadata) along with the usual information returned by LIST.

eli5.summary: When you ask for a list of folders, you may also want notes about each. This lets email programs get both in one request.

questions: how to get mailbox annotations in imap list
what does the metadata return option do
subtitle: Lets an email client ask for folder list and per-folder annotations in one IMAP command.

tldr.problem: An IMAP client that wants to show mailbox metadata, such as a color, has to list the mailboxes first and then send a GETMETADATA command for each one.
tldr.mechanism: The LIST-METADATA extension adds a METADATA return option to the extended LIST command, so the server sends each LIST response followed by METADATA responses for the requested annotations.
tldr.outcome: The client gets everything in a single command, saving bandwidth and avoiding the performance cost of many separate requests.

today: RFC 9590 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2024. It has not been obsoleted or updated, and it builds on the metadata mechanism in RFC 5464.

sections.title: The Problem and the Extension
sections.content:
IMAP clients sometimes fetch mailbox metadata, for example a color, to improve how mailboxes are displayed. Without this extension, the client must issue a LIST or LSUB command and then a GETMETADATA command for each mailbox found.

This document defines an extension to the IMAP LIST command identified by the capability string LIST-METADATA. It lets the client request mailbox annotations along with the information that LIST normally returns.
sections.eli5: Instead of asking one question to get the folder names and then many more to get notes on each folder, you ask once.

sections.title: The METADATA Return Option
sections.content:
RFC 5464 defines GETMETADATA. Doing many of those calls wastes bandwidth and can hurt performance when the client does not pipeline the requests. This document therefore adds a new return option, METADATA, to the extended LIST command.

For each listable mailbox that matches the list pattern and selection options, the server MUST return an untagged LIST response followed by one or more untagged METADATA responses with the requested annotations. These have the same syntax and meaning as responses to GETMETADATA on the same mailboxes. The server may put all annotations in one METADATA response or split them across several.

If the server cannot look up the annotations for a mailbox, it MAY drop that mailbox's METADATA response, and the LIST command still ends with a tagged OK.
sections.eli5: For every folder that fits your search, the server tells you its name and then the notes you asked for. If it cannot find the notes for one folder, it skips them and carries on.

sections.title: Examples and Syntax
sections.content:
The RFC's examples fetch a color annotation for top-level mailboxes. A mailbox whose annotation is unset gets a METADATA response with the value NIL. A mailbox such as bar that has children but is not itself a real mailbox gets no METADATA response.

A second example uses SUBSCRIBED RECURSIVEMATCH. The LIST response for foo is returned because it has matching children, but no METADATA response follows because foo itself does not match the selection criteria.

The formal syntax adds a single ABNF rule: return-option =/ "METADATA" SP "(" entry *(SP entry) ")", where the entry names come from RFC 5464.
sections.eli5: If a folder has no note yet, the answer is "nothing here". If a name is only a container for other folders, there are no notes to report.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
sections.content: The specification introduces no security concerns beyond those in RFC 5258 and RFC 5464, and no privacy concerns beyond those in RFC 5464. The RFC adds no new threats of its own.
sections.eli5: Asking for notes in the list does not let anyone see anything they could not already ask for.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA added the LIST-METADATA capability to the IMAP Capabilities registry. It also registered the METADATA option, of type RETURN, in the LIST-EXTENDED options registry. Its description is that it causes the LIST command to return METADATA responses in addition to LIST responses.
sections.eli5: The new feature got its official name written in the public list of IMAP features.

viz.caption: LIST WITH METADATA RETURN OPTION (from RFC 9590)

data.title: Extended LIST example (unwrapped)
data.code:
C: A01 LIST "" % RETURN (METADATA ("/shared/vendor/cmu/cyrus-imapd/color"))
S: * LIST () "." "INBOX"
S: * METADATA INBOX ("/shared/vendor/cmu/cyrus-imapd/color" "#b71c1c")
S: * LIST () "." "foo"
S: * METADATA "foo" ("/shared/vendor/cmu/cyrus-imapd/color" NIL)
S: * LIST (\NonExistent) "." "bar"
S: A01 OK List completed.
